summary: Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gualtherus Hendrik Mees was an indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge (M.A., ~1924–1928) and Leiden University (LL.D., ~1928–1935), where he also studied under Jean Philippe Vogel.

Buddhist studies scholar Guang Xing earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (~1999–2003) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He held posts at the University of Hong Kong (around 2003) and the University of British Columbia (2007).

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2004) and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.
Guankong worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Buddhist studies scholar Gudo Wafu Nishijima earned a law degree from the University of Tokyo, studied under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa, and founded Dogen Sangha International in 2007. He lectured at the University of Tokyo and Eastern Institute.

Gudrun Bühnemann works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna (~1975–1980) under Ernst Steinkellner, also studying under Michael Hahn. Since 1992, she has held a professorship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Indology and Buddhist studies scholar Gudrun Melzer completed her doctoral degrees at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. As attested in 2026, she holds positions at the University of Munich, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and IIBS.

Scholar of Indology and linguistics Guilherme de Vasconcelos Abreu studied at the University of Coimbra, under Abel Bergaigne, and under Martin Haug. He founded the Associação Promotora dos Estudos Orientais e Glóticos (1873) and taught Sanskrit at Curso Superior de Letras (1877).

Active in history and archaeology, Guillaume Le Gentil studied at the Faculté de théologie catholique de Paris and the Collège de France (~1745–1748). He held a post at the Paris Observatory from around 1748 to 1792.

Guillaume Oisel works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned a doctorate in linguistics from Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2006–2013) and served as a lecturer at the National University of San Marcos in 2019.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Indology and linguistics scholar Gunilla Gren-Eklund studied under Stig Wikander and Nils Simonsson (~1968–1976). She held an academic post at Uppsala University from around 1976 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from around 1926 to 1933 and subsequently held a post there from around 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun, a Buddhist and religious studies scholar, studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, learning under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery, attested in 2013.

Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyu Mitomo. He also studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, Zensho Kitagawa, Gyoko Iotani, Seiichi Kiritani, Koken Sasaki, Zuiei Ito, and Kosuke Nakazawa.

Gurii Stepanov specialized in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Seminary (~1896–1902) and Kazan Theological Academy (1902–1906), where he was appointed Docent of Kalmuk in 1909.

Gurinder Singh Mann, a religious studies and Indology scholar, earned degrees from Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia (PhD, ~1987–1993). He taught at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Kundan Kaur Kapany Chair at UC Santa Barbara (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Religious studies scholar Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga earned his doctorate at Leiden University (1893–1901). He was a professor at the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944) and later served as a docent at Utrecht University (1944–1957).

Buddhist and religious studies scholar Gustaaf Houtman earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, studying under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell. He served as Senior Teaching Fellow in anthropology and sociology at SOAS, attested in 2014.
